text:
marta_customer: Hey team — streaming responses on our Private deployment keep cutting out after ~12–18kB, client sees a partial chunk then reconnects. Repro'd with our web app behind corporate proxy + on-prem ingress. Happening across multiple models. Anyone seen this?

jess_support: Hi Marta — sorry you're hitting this. Which deployment mode is it? Private via customer VPC or on-prem package? Can you paste the root request id from the API logs?

marta_customer: It's Private (on-prem package) routed through our corp proxy/load-balancer (F5). Root request id: req_202603140912_abc123. Logs show the server sends several SSE "data: ..." events then connection closes. Client shows `net::ERR_INCOMPLETE_CHUNKED_ENCODING` sometimes.

raj_infra: Thanks — ERR_INCOMPLETE_CHUNKED_ENCODING usually means the TCP stream ended mid-chunk or the proxy buffered/re-wrote chunking. Two immediate suspects: MTU/MSS clamping causing segments to be dropped, or the proxy closing idle SSE streams after a threshold.

sam_network: Also check if TLS offload on the load balancer is doing HTTP buffering. Some F5 configs will buffer the upstream response until full chunk arrives and then drop if it hits a size threshold. What's your LB config for `proxy-send-timeout` / `idle-timeout`?

marta_customer: LB idle timeout is 60s. We see disconnects within ~10–20s while tokens are still streaming. The client does automatic reconnect and then usually resumes but we've observed repeated partial outputs (some tokens missing).

jess_support: Can you reproduce with curl from inside the same network (bypassing the browser)? Try:

`````
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://private.example.com/v1/streams/generate
`````

Use `-N` to disable buffering. Does the behavior differ from the browser?

marta_customer: Good call — from a bastion inside the VPC, `curl -N` shows continuous SSE events and no abrupt close. From a workstation behind corp proxy curl closes the stream around the same size as the browser.

raj_infra: That strongly suggests the corporate proxy/LB is the root cause. Two further repro steps: 1) run tcpdump on the on-prem ingress and capture the FIN/RST timing, 2) test lowering MTU on the bastion to match corporate path MTU and see if the drop shifts.

sam_network: If MTU mismatch is happening, you might see consistent packet retransmits and an MSS clamp on the path. For F5 we often see `tcp-mss adjust` rules. Try `sudo ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1400` on the bastion and repro.

marta_customer: Will try MTU trick now. Quick Q: do SSE streams count as multiple billed requests or a single request? Because we have many partial reconnects and our billing spike looked odd.

billing_bot: Billing note: We meter per request/session and per output tokens. For a streaming request that reconnects and resumes with the same logical request id, our platform attempts to attribute tokens to the original session when possible. If the client reopens a brand-new request without replaying the `stream_resume_id`, tokens may be billed as separate events. If you want us to audit the specific req_ IDs we can do a one-off refund.

jess_support: Marta — please send the full set of request_ids from the failed sessions and we'll route to billing. Meanwhile focus on reproducing without the corporate proxy. If MTU fix helps, we can recommend two mitigations: 1) set upstream keepalives and disable aggressive HTTP buffering on the LB, 2) for Private on-prem doc update: recommend MTU >= 1400 between ingress and worker nodes for SSE workloads.

marta_customer: MTU 1400 reduced the disconnects a lot — streaming now completes more often. When it still breaks it's always when a corp proxy appliance does deep packet inspect and inserts a small response header, which seems to cause chunk boundaries to change mid-stream.

raj_infra: That matches past cases — intermediate proxies that rewrite responses can invalidate chunk framing. For a durable solution: configure your F5 to pass-through `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and disable response buffering for those paths, or terminate SSE at the LB and proxy with WebSocket tunneling.

sam_network: Also consider increasing LB keepalive to >120s and set `proxy_read_timeout` to a high value. For nginx-ish proxies, `proxy_buffering off; chunked_transfer_encoding on;` helps.

marta_customer: Thanks. Last thing — we also observed occasional `401` mid-stream when the token auto-rotated in our SPA. Could that cause an immediate close?

jess_support: Yes — if the authorization header is invalid mid-stream our platform will close the SSE with a 401 and include a final event with `error: auth_expired`. To avoid that, keep a refresh flow that opens a new stream rather than mutating headers mid-connection. We can add a clearer final SSE event for expired tokens in the next runtime patch.

ops_bot: FYI filed an internal follow-up: INFR-5962 — add clearer `auth_expired` SSE termination event and doc callouts for proxies and MTU on Private deployments.

marta_customer: Appreciate the help. I'll share configs and request_ids in a DM and open a ticket with our LB team to change buffering.

jess_support: Great. Please paste `req_` ids and a pcap if you capture one. We'll escalate to eng-runtime if we see server-side FINs without client-side RSTs. :+1:
